subject: Arabic
title: The Arabic Alphabet
body:
The Qur'an was revealed in Arabic. We start with its 28 letters:

ا ب ت ث ج ح خ د ذ ر ز س ش ص ض ط ظ ع غ ف ق ك ل م ن هـ و ي

Practise saying each letter aloud. Letters change shape depending on where they are in a word — beginning, middle or end.

Try it: Find Alif (ا), Baa (ب) and Taa (ت) in the line above.

subject: Duas
title: Duas for Every Day
body:
Before eating: Bismillah — In the name of Allah.

After eating: Alhamdulillah — All praise is for Allah.

Before sleeping: Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya — In Your name, O Allah, I die and I live.

For parents: Rabbi-r hamhuma kama rabbayani sagheera — My Lord, have mercy on them as they raised me when I was small. (Qur'an 17:24)

subject: Salah
title: What is Salah?
body:
Salah is the prayer Muslims perform five times a day. It is how we talk to Allah, thank Him and ask Him for help.

The five daily prayers: Fajr (dawn), Dhuhr (midday), Asr (afternoon), Maghrib (sunset), Isha (night).

Before Salah we make Wudu (washing) so we are clean for prayer.

subject: Qur'an
title: Reading the Qur'an with Tajweed
body:
Tajweed means reading the Qur'an correctly and beautifully, the way it was revealed.

Key rules to start:

  • Makharij — each letter comes from its correct place in the mouth/throat.
  • Madd — stretch long vowels (2, 4 or 6 counts).
  • Noon Sakinah rules: Izhar, Idgham, Iqlab, Ikhfa.

Rule of learning: a little, correctly, every day beats a lot, rushed.

subject: Qur'an
title: Surah Al-Fatiha — The Opening
body:
Al-Fatiha is the first Surah of the Qur'an and is read in every unit (rak'ah) of Salah.

بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ ﴿١﴾ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ ﴿٢﴾ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ ﴿٣﴾ مَالِكِ يَوْمِ الدِّينِ ﴿٤﴾ إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ وَإِيَّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُ ﴿٥﴾ اهْدِنَا الصِّرَاطَ الْمُسْتَقِيمَ ﴿٦﴾ صِرَاطَ الَّذِينَ أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ غَيْرِ الْمَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا الضَّالِّينَ ﴿٧﴾

Meaning in brief: All praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds, the Most Merciful. You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help. Guide us on the Straight Path.

subject: Seerah
title: Seerah: The Prophet ﷺ in Makkah
body:
Prophet Muhammad ﷺ was born in Makkah in the Year of the Elephant (about 570 CE). Known as Al-Amin (the Trustworthy), he received the first revelation at age 40 in Cave Hira: “Read, in the name of your Lord who created.” (96:1)

For 13 years in Makkah he called people to worship Allah alone, with patience through hardship, before the Hijrah to Madina.

subject: Salah
title: Salah Step by Step
body:
1. Intention & Takbir — Face the Qiblah, raise hands, say Allahu Akbar.
  2. Qiyam (standing) — Recite Al-Fatiha and a Surah.
  3. Ruku (bowing) — Bow, hands on knees: Subhana Rabbiyal Azeem (3x).
  4. Stand — Sami Allahu liman hamidah, Rabbana lakal hamd.
  5. Sujood (prostration) — Forehead to the ground: Subhana Rabbiyal A'la (3x). Sit, then prostrate again.
  6. Tashahhud & Salam — Sit, recite Tashahhud and Durood, end with Salam to right and left.

Two rak'ahs complete Fajr; Dhuhr, Asr and Isha have four; Maghrib has three.

subject: Arabic
title: Arabic Reading: Vowels & Joining
body:
Short vowels (Harakat): Fatha ( َ a), Kasra ( ِ i), Damma ( ُ u). Long vowels use Alif, Waw and Ya as stretchers.

Sukoon ( ْ ) means no vowel; Shaddah ( ّ ) doubles a letter. Most letters join to the next letter; ا د ذ ر ز و never join forward.

Practise: كَتَبَ (kataba — he wrote), قَرَأَ (qara'a — he read), نُور (noor — light).

subject: Qur'an
title: Adults: Starting the Qur'an from Zero
body:
It's never too late. Every adult learner in our class started with the alphabet.

Your path: 1) Letters & sounds, 2) Joined letters & vowels, 3) Short Surahs (Al-Fatiha, Al-Ikhlas, Al-Falaq, An-Nas), 4) Reading from the Mushaf, 5) Tajweed refinement.

Goal for month one: recognise all 28 letters and read three-letter words. Small daily practice — 10 minutes — wins.
